name: m4-leyden-l2-scala
description: L2 of the Leyden evaluation (scala `LEYDEN.md`, branch claude/leyden-bench-eval): does a fork started from an AOT cache (JEP 483/515: cached classes plus the training fork's method profiles) measure the same steady state as a cold fork?

The smoke test showed cached forks with ~8,000 methods held at tier 2 (the training policy's lukewarm hold: methods trained at tier ≤3 stay at tier 2 until their counts exceed the training run's) and ~800 fewer C2 methods. `aot-short` trains on 3 iterations, so the measured fork's counts pass the training counts early and the hold releases. Build `1e85ab8eba`, stock JDK 26 integration build, m4. Copy of `leyden-l2-scala`, which the laptop's load stopped in round 1. Each variant names the same checkout, so each gets its own snapshot and its own caches.

variantDescriptions.aot: one cache, trained by a fork with the same JMH arguments (`-wi 8 -i 5`)
variantDescriptions.aot-short: one cache, trained by a 3-iteration fork (`-wi 2 -i 1`)
